articles.title: Medial Epicondyle Morphology and Medial Elbow Gapping in High School Baseball Players: Implications for Throwing-Related Elbow Pain.
articles.authors: Nishi R, Ogawa T, Kubota A, Obokata Y, Aoyagi M, Furushima K, et al.
articles.population: High school baseball players competing at national tournament level
articles.outcomes: Medial epicondyle morphology (protrusion, fragmentation, irregularity) assessed by ultrasound; medial elbow gapping at rest and under valgus stress; throwing-related elbow pain (current, within past year, or historical)
articles.take_home: Medial elbow gapping measured under stress was linked to elbow pain experienced in the past year, but structural changes to the medial epicondyle were not associated with increased gapping. This suggests that how the elbow moves under stress may be more important than its shape in identifying recent throwing-related elbow pain.

articles.title: Is the Presence, Increased Number, or Certain Category of Patient-Reported Allergies Associated with a Poor Outcome after Total Shoulder Arthroplasty?
articles.authors: Khoo KJ, Dasari SP, Chin EK, Palumbo NE, Matsen FA 3rd, Hsu JE, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 547 patients (302 reported one or more allergies)
articles.outcomes: 2-year Simple Shoulder Test scores, percentage of maximal possible improvement, and revision rate
articles.take_home: Having allergies did not affect shoulder surgery outcomes overall, but patients reporting two or more allergies had worse results than those with none or one allergy. Allergies to medications other than antibiotics or painkillers were linked to poorer outcomes.

articles.title: Defining A Successful Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review of Clinically Relevant Outcome Metrics.
articles.authors: Khilnani TK, Megerian MF, Xu T, Yousef M, Al-Thani MS, Taylor SA, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) including ASES score, Simple Shoulder Test, Constant-Murley score, and VAS; minimal clinically important difference (MCID), patient acceptable symptom state (PASS), and substantial clinical benefit (SCB)
articles.take_home: There is no agreed standard for measuring success after shoulder replacement surgery. The ASES score is most commonly used, but how clinically meaningful improvements are defined varies widely between studies, so results cannot easily be compared.

articles.title: Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty with a Glenoid-Sided Lateralized Prosthesis and Concomitant Latissimus Dorsi Transfer Is Associated with Early Proximal Humeral Osseous Erosion Without Superior Functional Outcomes.
articles.authors: Hung VT, Kucharik MP, Konapala A, Schmidt RC, Likine E, Ranson WA, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort comparison with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients with massive irreparable rotator cuff tears and preoperative external rotation deficit undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, active external rotation, proximal humeral osseous erosion on imaging
articles.take_home: Adding a latissimus dorsi tendon transfer to reverse shoulder arthroplasty did not improve shoulder function or external rotation better than surgery alone, but was associated with early bone erosion at the top of the upper arm bone. Both treatments significantly improved overall function and rotation.

articles.title: Medium Term Reoperation Rates after Primary Total Elbow Arthroplasty at a Single Institution: 303 Cases.
articles.authors: Singh A, Fiandeiro M, Satalich J, Shi B, Markmann C, Fellheimer H, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total elbow arthroplasty for any indication
articles.sample_size: 303 patients (63 male, 240 female); mean age 68.4 years; mean follow-up 4.6 years
articles.outcomes: Reoperation rates, infection rates, causes of reoperation (loosening, wear, fracture), surgical approaches
articles.take_home: One in five patients needed another operation within about four and a half years after total elbow replacement, most commonly due to infection or the implant becoming loose. Despite better designs and techniques, elbow replacements still face significant durability challenges.

articles.title: Shear-Wave Elastography for Assessing the Histological Characteristics of Torn Rotator Cuff Tendons.
articles.authors: Chen V, Beretov J, Bilog AM, Changbean Kang E, Sima S, Bilbrough J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with torn supraspinatus tendons undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Association between shear-wave elastography stiffness values (kPa) and histological features including cellularity, collagen organisation, tenocyte morphology, vascularisation and glycosaminoglycan content assessed by Bonar score
articles.take_home: Shear-wave elastography can detect specific tissue damage patterns in torn rotator cuff tendons, particularly areas with mixed cellularity and disorganised collagen. This non-invasive imaging technique may help doctors assess tendon quality before and after surgery.

articles.title: Implant migration and clinical outcomes with cemented vs cementless Motec cups in total trapeziometacarpal arthroplasty: a 10-year prospective RSA cohort study of 69 patients.
articles.authors: Rautio E, Stilling M, Hansen TB, Thillemann JK
articles.study_type: Prospective comparative cohort study with radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing total trapeziometacarpal arthroplasty with Motec cups
articles.sample_size: 69 patients (22 cementless cups, 47 cemented cups); 13 at 10-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Cup migration measured by radiostereometric analysis at 3 weeks, 3 months, 1, 2, 5, and 10 years; clinical outcomes including pain, grip strength, and Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand score; cup revision rates
articles.take_home: After 10 years, cemented and cementless Motec cups showed similar amounts of movement, though 25 cups overall needed revision mainly due to loosening. Cups that were revised moved more in the first year or two, and patients with worsening pain and function scores were more likely to need revision surgery.

articles.title: The impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists on postoperative outcomes following rotator cuff repair.
articles.authors: Choudhury A, Slusarczyk S, Mathson L, Van Boxtel M, LoGiudice A, Hanley J
articles.population: Adults with type II diabetes undergoing rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: 90-day medical complications, surgical complications, postoperative stiffness, respiratory complications, urinary tract infection, and healthcare utilisation
articles.take_home: GLP-1 agonist medicines used before rotator cuff repair surgery were not found to increase the risk of problems after surgery, suggesting it may be safe to continue these medicines around the time of surgery. However, the researchers say larger prospective studies are needed to confirm this finding.

articles.title: Radial extracorporeal shockwave therapy (rESWT) for patients with chronic lateral elbow tendinopathy (tennis elbow): A double-blinded randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Wheeler PC, Tattersall C, Calver R
articles.population: Patients with chronic lateral elbow tendinopathy (tennis elbow)
articles.outcomes: Self-reported pain (primary outcome), validated patient-reported outcome measures. Follow-up at 6 weeks, 3 months and 6 months.
articles.take_home: Both groups improved similarly over six months, with pain reducing by 52% at six months regardless of shockwave therapy dose. The study found no extra benefit from higher-dose shockwave therapy compared to minimal-dose therapy when combined with a home exercise programme.
